title: Write the checker for the one-gateway rule
ask: Two of the three rules that keep replays reproducible are grepped on every page load and hold today. The third — that every world mutation goes through SimWorld.apply_action — has no checker at all: a renderer writing straight into the grid would compile and pass both suites, and the break would stay silent until phase-4 bot training failed on corrupt data. Write a static check over world/, entities/ and player/ for assignments into SimWorld's fields, and add it as a fifth CI job.
first_action: Read docs/ARCHITECTURE.md's layer rules and systems/sim/sim_world.gd, then write the check and prove it catches a deliberate violation.
source_message: Two of the three rules that keep replays reproducible are grepped on every page load and hold today. The third — that every world mutation goes through SimWorld.apply_action — has no checker at all: a renderer writing straight into the grid would compile and pass both suites, and the break would stay silent until phase-4 bot training failed on corrupt data. Write a static check over world/, entities/ and player/ for assignments into SimWorld's fields, and add it as a fifth CI job.
result: This attempt did not finish — it used all the turns it was given, mid-edit. What it had already changed did land, and the check below is what the chief of staff made of it.

check.summary: The checker, its self-test, the fifth CI job and the HQ wiring all landed and read correctly, but a compiled .pyc is staged with the diff, a whole-field reassignment like `sim.tiles = ...` slips past the write regex, and CLAUDE.md still says CI runs four jobs; the worker sent no reply, and I could not execute the script from this seat, so run it once before committing.

findings.what: Compiled Python bytecode is staged as part of the change; nothing in .gitignore excludes __pycache__, so it would be committed
findings.fix: Drop the file from the index, delete it, and add `__pycache__/` to .gitignore in the same commit

findings.what: Replacing a whole sim field (`sim.tiles = []`, `sim.clock = x`, `sim.actors = {}`) is not caught: the write regex requires `[` or `.` after the field name, so the bluntest possible violation passes
findings.fix: Accept `\s*=` after the field as well as `[` and `.`, and plant a bare `sim.tiles = []` line in _self_test so the gap cannot reopen

findings.what: CLAUDE.md still says CI runs unit, integration, robot session and the benchmark; the fifth job is not mentioned, and ARCHITECTURE.md's S-3 paragraph does not say the rule is now enforced
findings.fix: Add the gateway check to the CI sentence in CLAUDE.md and one sentence at ARCHITECTURE.md's S-3 rule naming tools/check_gateway.py as its enforcement

findings.what: No worker reply came back and the checker was not executed in this review (sandbox blocked python3); the static read says the real scan passes with six waived lines in farm.gd and no ungated writes in entities/ or player/, and the self-test's expected mutator list matches sim_world.gd, but that is a reading, not a run
findings.fix: Run `python3 tools/check_gateway.py --self-test` and `python3 tools/check_gateway.py` before committing, alongside the two suites
